Inter-assessor agreement

This assessment is DUAL — two assessors from different model families, the second asked blind. The agreement rate is withheld pending adjudication. Both readers were given this review’s decision rule; an earlier version of this sentence said the blinding had withheld it, and that was wrong. What the 10 domain comparison(s) show is a reading difference that runs in OPPOSITE directions by domain — on domains 1 to 3 the second assessor more often declines to judge at all, and on domains 4 and 5 it more often judges low. A single agreement rate averages those two behaviours into one number that describes neither. Both assessors’ per-result judgements are shown in the table above, unadjudicated, and neither is this review’s finding. No adjudication has been performed, so this review holds no final risk-of-bias judgement for these results.

not recorded on the page this object was extracted from

The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason.

The registered primary of both trials is a median percent change from baseline to Week 12 in fasting serum triglycerides -- that wording is on both registrations. This pool is a mean difference. In populations selected for triglycerides above 500 mg/dL (MARINE) and above 200 mg/dL (ANCHOR) the mean and the median diverge by construction, so this pooled value answers a question neither trial asked. The estimate is not changed here: correcting a summary statistic changes what the published number means and that is a content decision.

Both trials registered three arms -- placebo, AMR101 2 g/day and AMR101 4 g/day. This object records two. A dose arm was selected and the selection is recorded nowhere. A review that selects among registered options without recording the selection has made an analytic decision that cannot be audited from its own output.

Why this is not an adjudicated disputeA blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. That would ordinarily be a dispute to adjudicate. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred ; the guidance is being applied.
What the registry gives and does notA ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: Randomized`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
How this maps to the tool s algorithmThe tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a domain judgement of some concerns. This project writes no information on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the overall at some concerns. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
What does not changeNo overall rating and no GRADE CERTAINTY moves. All 51 judgements were already capped at some concerns or HIGH by another no information domain.
And this one also inferred concealment from arm balanceThis judgement cited, in addition, that the arm sizes are balanced and that this is what a concealed sequence produces. That is an inference, not a registry fact. Balanced arms are consistent with concealment and do not establish it, and RoB 2 signalling question 1.3 asks whether baseline differences suggest a problem -- a different question from whether concealment was adequate. The entry states in its own words that the mechanism was never read.
This does not replace the stored judgementThis is the judgement the published algorithm proposes from the signalling responses named here. It does not replace the stored `judgement` beside it, and nothing reads it yet. The tool itself says its algorithms "provide proposed judgements, but users should verify these and change them if they feel this is appropriate" -- so this is an input to a person, not an output to a reader.
Why this profile is not the empagliflozin profileempagliflozin-hf's two results are adjudicated time-to-event composites: missing outcome data LOW because censoring absorbs withdrawal, measurement of the outcome LOW because a blinded committee adjudicates, selection of the reported result LOW because one primary was registered and reported. This result is a fixed-timepoint laboratory value: missing outcome data is no information because a missed Week-12 visit is a missing value rather than shortened follow-up, measurement of the outcome is LOW for a different reason -- an automated assay -- and selection of the reported result is some concerns because the pooled statistic is not the registered one. Four of five domains differ in judgement OR in reason. An assessment that came out the same would have been evidence of copying rather than assessing.
The arm roles on this object are invertedBoth trials record 'Placebo' as the treatment arm and 'AMR101 (ethyl icosapentate) - 4 g/day' as the control -- already on the open list. This assessment does not inherit that labelling: every domain is judged against what the registration says the trial did.
Registered statistic is a median and this pools a meanBoth registered primaries describe a median percent change from baseline to Week 12. This object stores and pools a mean difference. In a population selected for triglycerides above 500 mg/dL the two diverge by construction, so the pooled -25.84 is not the registered estimand of either trial. Not corrected -- it changes what the published number means.
And it bounds a finding of oursClass 94 records assessor 2 saying no information on the randomisation process/deviations from the intended intervention/missing outcome data `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are the randomisation process=some concerns on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.
The rate is still conditional on the same allow listBoth numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.
Which risk of bias domains drove the ratingWhere a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: selection of the reported result on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.

Title

Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. title

Abstract

Question. In adults with hypertriglyceridemia, does AMR101 (ethyl icosapentate) - 4 g/day compared with placebo affect difference between amr101 (ethyl icosapentate) and placebo treatment groups in triglyceride lowering effect?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects model with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect: mean difference -25.8 (-36.8 to -14.8) across 2 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; and no statistical heterogeneity was detected (I-squared 64.2%), though heterogeneity cannot be reliably assessed with two trials.3

Introduction

Background. This review asks: In adults with hypertriglyceridemia, does AMR101 (ethyl icosapentate) - 4 g/day compared with placebo affect difference between amr101 (ethyl icosapentate) and placebo treatment groups in triglyceride lowering effect? It pools 2 randomised trials. The outcome pooled is Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect.1

Methods — synthesis

For difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) , following . 2 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 1 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.4

Results

The pooled mean difference for difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect was -25.8 (-36.8 to -14.8) across 2 trials.1

Noted on this pool. The registered primary of both trials is a median percent change from baseline to Week 12 in fasting serum triglycerides -- that wording is on both registrations. This pool is a mean difference. In populations selected for triglycerides above 500 mg/dL (marine) and above 200 mg/dL (anchor) the mean and the median diverge by construction, so this pooled value answers a question neither trial asked. The estimate is not changed here: correcting a summary statistic changes what the published number means and that is a content decision. Both trials registered three arms -- placebo, AMR101 2 g/day and AMR101 4 g/day. This object records two. A dose arm was selected and the selection is recorded nowhere. A review that selects among registered options without recording the selection has made an analytic decision that cannot be audited from its own output.2

The trials' results were loosely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 64.2%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 43.2, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 2.79, on degrees of freedom 1.3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is stored verbatim on this review object at `results.by_outcome.<outcome>.r_output.verbatim`. It is not reproduced as an Extended data section in this article; an earlier version of this sentence said it was, and no such section exists.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 at the level of each reported result, by two assessors reading independently. Their judgements differ on 1 of the 2 results and no adjudication has been performed, so this review holds no final risk-of-bias judgement for these results. Assessor 1 recorded: 2 at some concerns. Assessor 2 recorded: 1 at some concerns, 1 at no information. Both are shown in the risk-of-bias table; neither is the review's finding. The per-domain judgements behind them are recorded with the extracted data.1

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

This certainty rating is pending, not rated. It rests on a risk-of-bias judgement that this review has not finalised: two assessors read every contributing result independently, they disagree, and no adjudication has been performed, so this review holds no final risk-of-bias judgement for these results. Cochrane rates certainty per outcome by aggregating the risk-of-bias judgements of the results contributing to it, so a certainty rating cannot be more final than the risk-of-bias assessment it reads. The rating this object currently records, and the steps behind it, are shown below as the work so far rather than as this review's answer. No level is published for this outcome -- not the recorded one, not a more cautious one, and not a midpoint -- because choosing one would be the judgement that has not been made.3

Certainty VERY_LOW. The risk-of-bias domain reads the per-result RoB 2 assessments made 2026-08-20 and named above, not a topic-level summary; indirectness reads the estimand findings recorded on this pool.4

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: selection of the reported result on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.5

difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering EffectPending2HIGHthe steps taken so far, not a final rating: risk of bias: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s) -- both results are some concerns and the driver is not empagliflozin's. selection of the reported result is some concerns in its own right: the registered primary is a median percent change and this pool is a mean difference, and both trials registered three arms where the object records two. deviations from the intended intervention and missing outcome data are additionally no information -- and missing outcome data here is a live threat rather than a formality, because a week-12 laboratory value is missing when a participant leaves, where a time-to-event result absorbs the same withdrawal by censoring. (rating: serious); inconsistency: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s) -- I-squared is 64.2% with tau-squared 43.19 over k=2. Handbook 10.10.2 warns against reading I-squared mechanically, and at this k the estimate is imprecise -- but the point estimates themselves differ materially and the direction of the finding does not rest on the statistic alone. (rating: serious); indirectness: LOW to VERY_LOW, down 1 level(s) -- the pooled quantity is not the registered quantity. Both registrations describe the primary as a median percent change from baseline to week 12 in fasting serum triglycerides; this pool is a mean difference. In populations selected on a triglyceride threshold -- above 500 mg/dL in marine, above 200 in anchor -- the mean and the median diverge by construction, which is precisely why a trialist reports a median. The pool therefore answers a question neither trial asked, and that is an indirectness fact, not a footnote. Compounded by a dose arm selected from three registered arms with the selection recorded nowhere. (rating: serious); imprecision: down 1 level(s) -- k=2, and the interval -36.84 to -14.84 spans a 22-point range on a percentage change. Two trials of 229 and 702 participants do not meet an optimal information size for an effect reported as a percentage of a skewed baseline. Handbook 15.6.2. (rating: serious); publication bias: not rated down -- not assessed rather than assessed as ABSENT. Funnel-plot asymmetry and its tests are uninformative below about ten studies -- Handbook 13.3.5.4 -- and these pools carry two or three. 'Undetected' here means nobody looked with an instrument that could see, not that publication bias is unlikely. Not rated down, because rating down on an unmeasurable domain would invent a defect. Limitations

What this review does not give a clinician: any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.1
